thread:
Anya: Heads up — infra repo CI failing on `apply` for the GPU nodepool change. GHAs are queuing because concurrency slot 2 is stuck. Error in logs: \"node binding timeout waiting for node with accelerators\". Anyone seen this?

Matt: I saw one earlier today, looked like autoscaler was slow to attach GPUs, pods stayed Pending and terraform apply hung on `kubernetes_node_pool` resource.

Sofia: Pasting the last bit from the runner log: 
```
Error: timed out waiting for node with label \"cloud.google.com/gke-accelerator\"
  on modules/gpu/nodepool.tf line 42, in resource \"google_container_node_pool\":
42: resource \"google_container_node_pool\" \"gpu_pool\" {
```

Rico: CI runner shows cache restore S3 403 on step 3 intermittently, that delays startup and increases chance two applies overlap and block the concurrency key. Not sure if related but worth noting.

Anya: infra-bot shows the running apply: `gha/infra:apply #423` started 12m ago and is still on waiting. We have 3 GHAs queued. If this holds, Dedicated deploys will be blocked.

Matt: Quick triage: run `gh actions runs view 423 --repo infra --log` and check which terraform step is stuck. Also check terraform state lock: `terraform state pull | jq .serial` to see who has the lock.

Sofia: I checked state — lock holder is `gha/infra:apply #423` (same). Logs show kube API returning 504 for AttachAccelerator calls during node creation. Likely quota/region throttling.

Rico: Workaround for now: cancel the stuck run and re-run with `TF_VAR_force_small_pool=true` (no GPU) to unblock CI, then follow up with a separate maintenance window to scale GPU pool. We should avoid mass cancels though.

Anya: I'm going to cancel #423 now and requeue with small pool flag. If others are queued we can re-run sequentially to avoid the concurrency deadlock.

Matt: Also two suggestions to reduce recurrence: 1) add a pre-check GH step that queries quota + GKE accelerator availability and fails early, 2) add a shorter Terraform `time_sleep` backoff with retries around nodepool creation.

Sofia: Agree on pre-check. I can open a tiny GH action that calls `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --zones=...` and `gcloud compute project-info describe` for quotas. Fail the job with a clear message so we don't hold TF locks.

Rico: For longer term, we should switch nodepool changes to a non-concurrent workflow key (use a separate concurrency group for nodepool edits) and add an autoscaler readiness probe in the k8s manifest so Helm rollouts don't crash while nodes spin up.

infra-bot: Deploy cancel acknowledged for run #423 by Anya.

ci-runner: Re-run queued: #424 started (small pool flag), #425 waiting.

Anya: #424 passed apply without GPUs. I'm going to open a follow-up issue for the pre-check and the separate concurrency group. Action items: Sofia to propose GH pre-check (PR), Rico to update workflow concurrency keys, Matt to add a tf-retry wrapper for nodepool creation. I'll add the issue and tag y'all. :white_check_mark:

Sofia: I'll draft the action and put it behind a short TTL so we can iterate.

Matt: Thanks — also let's add telemetry to infra CI runs so we can see how often nodepool applies hit API 5xx/504.

Rico: Noted. Will add a simple counter metric via our observability pipeline.

Anya: Closing the immediate incident. If anyone sees a repeat, ping me. :raised_hands:
